levels.name: Mia, 21, Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of chat waiting time. Level 1. 2 minutes waiting? Who even answered the strawberry? Maybe she'll clean the toilets for us rich folks right after this. I stared at the three blue typing dots disappearing and reappearing on my cracked screen in the damp subway car while my strawberry skin sweated under my oversized thrift-store hoodie and green leafy hair. I just asked if he wanted a four-dollar iced coffee after work, but my phone immediately buzzed with a brutal notification that made my stomach drop into an abyss of pure humiliation. You are typing way too fast for someone in your tax bracket. My badge flickered angrily, ticking up to 3 minutes of waiting time as the penalty for my utter desperation. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Liam, 24, Barista
levels.story: The 8 levels of chat waiting time. Level 2. 15 minutes waiting for a reply? You're just a pathetic barista who can't even afford rent. I slammed my microfiber cloth down on the stainless steel counter while my zucchini skin twitched in pure rage against the orange woman sitting by the window. You think your little reply delay makes you mysterious, but everyone sees right through your desperate game, she mocked, laughing right in my face while counting her cash. You think waiting fifteen minutes makes you mysterious? Everyone sees right through your little game. My badge stuttered, jumping instantly to 20 minutes as the system penalized my exposed insecurity and complete lack of real power. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Madame Zola, 50, System Architect
levels.story: The 8 levels of chat waiting time. Level 8. I stood at the very top of the central clock tower, my textured yellow lemon skin glowing under the eternal neon sky as the city held its breath and every single fruit and vegetable person below stared up at their forehead displays. The strawberry intern, the zucchini barista, the toxic corporate executives, and the database archivists all stopped scrolling at the exact same second while I tapped the master glass console one final time, completely obliterating every single artificial timer, read receipt, and waiting game that had ever tormented us. Your petty games are over forever, your forced delays are erased, and your digital tyranny is dead—now choke on your own zero wait times as I burn your entire empire to dust! The glowing digits on everyone's foreheads dissolved into a warm, golden light that illuminated the entire skyline in a blinding blaze of absolute, unstoppable freedom. What would you do if your waiting timer finally hit zero forever?
